speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, the fact is that their needs are varied based on their stages of growth, the sectors within which they operated and also, to some extent, the markets in which they are venturing into beyond Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And this variation is also accentuated by the fact that there are different types of growth opportunities, digitalisation and technology change, which have a differential impact on the various sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The fact is that the programmes and schemes are available to all enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The ITMs bring them together in particular sectors because there are certain objectives around that but, in general, the accessibility is open to all.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I also want to address the point about micro SMEs because they are an important segment of the economy and they have much potential.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and also Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Desmond Choo highlighted this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Louis Ng cited survey findings indicating that few SMEs want to venture overseas due to concerns over insufficient funding, unfamiliarity and heightened competition in foreign markets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, as I highlighted earlier, there are also surveys by SCCCI and DP Information Group (SME Development Survey), which found that a significant proportion of our enterprises have, in fact, prioritised internationalisation and have plans to do so in the next few years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This becomes then a battle of the surveys, and which is right and which is wrong.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The reality of what it shows is that the terrain is uneven.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, whilst we are making the best of efforts to reach out to all our companies, some, depending on their stage of development, their sector and so on, will have a differential response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Some might even not have addressed these issues because they are so used to some other aspects of their business.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I also want to say that it is quite understandable that SMEs have concerns when venturing abroad because that is not without risks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On Enterprise Singapore's part, it will sustain and, where necessary, step up efforts to help companies that are facing challenges in financial management, brand building and product promotions, points that Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Saktiandi  Supaat have highlighted.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we have also worked with the TACs and companies to encourage greater collaboration in sharing of experiences so that they can enter markets more effectively, perhaps in partnership or at least learning from each other's experience, so that the pathway is a bit less difficult.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I do want to make one point.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ultimately, each entrepreneur has to weigh the risk-reward balance of any new venture before making a decision.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is the very essence of entrepreneurship and it is not something that can be supplanted by any Government agency or support programme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is important that whilst we have this architecture of schemes and programmes to support our enterprises, our entrepreneurs have to step up, make the assessments and take the decision.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Leon Perera made a good point, which is that, at the end of the day, the levels of ambition may be different and also the appetite for risks, and we respect that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, it is more about individual companies and their leaders making the choice and then benefiting from the appropriate schemes that are available from our economic agencies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I want to turn next to a set of questions around the programmes and schemes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Various Members have raised these questions and they have asked whether the Government schemes will be streamlined, if not now, then in the future, and in the process of the transition.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Generally, the streamlining of Government grants is an ongoing process because we want to ensure policy efficacy, meaning that it is achieving its desired or stated objective; and also to ensure accessibility for businesses and, importantly, staying relevant in the context of the different circumstances.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, for example, there have been changes made to some of the processes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And it includes grants administered not just by MTI agencies but also others like BCA's Building Information Model Fund.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The plan is to add more grants to this portal progressively.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we share the objective of wanting to make things simpler for our companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Enterprise Singapore will continue the review of its touchpoints, processes and schemes for that purpose.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But at the same time, I agree with the point made by Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that whilst we have a quest for ease of access and efficiency in the administration of Government grants, they should not come at the expense of efficient and effective safeguards.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Government takes a strong stance against any case of fraud or abuse and will take stern enforcement action after investigations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Internal control systems are reviewed regularly and the lessons learnt, especially from some incidents of abuse, are incorporated to prevent future irregularities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not foolproof but it is an important part of the process of continuing to ensure that safeguards are in place.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the specific point about the transition, because the schemes are being administered by SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore today, and after 1 April, by Enterprise Singapore, the important element here is not so much to have an audit today but ensuring that there is a clear audit trail because all the officers will be working in the new organisation in one form or another, and it is important that we have the data, the analysis and the audit trails so that if there is a need for verification, it can be done, regardless of when that need arises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I want to assure Mr Louis Ng that Enterprise Singapore will continue SPRING Singapore's close collaboration with our agencies, such as the National Environment Agency (NEA) in order to encourage the SMEs to adopt efficient energy practices in their businesses, as well as to support the adoption of standards to ensure their sustainability.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These practices, and I want to echo the point that Mr Louis Ng and others have made, they are not just relevant for the reason of sustainability of the environment but also because they make good business sense.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, many enterprises today differentiate themselves on the basis of their sustainable practices.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh's query was whether there has been a good take-up rate of the programmes that support our local enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As I said in the Second Reading speech earlier, both SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore have been able to reach out to more and more enterprises over the years and there has been good traction.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think this is something that will continue under Enterprise Singapore and it will reach out to more companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will share more details on any changes to the suite of schemes and grants at the upcoming Budget and Committee of Supply debates.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Before I move on, I do want to highlight one thing.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As we listened to the comments and ideas made by many of the Members who spoke today, I think the inherent tensions in some of our aspirations become quite apparent.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the one hand, we want one organisation because that would make it easy for everyone to know where to go to get what kind of help; on the other hand, we want the nimbleness and flexibility of small organisations because they can move around and be quicker in their response.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the one hand, we want customised programmes to help companies which have got specific needs and they have got higher ambitions or greater risk appetite; on the other hand, we want broad-based, easy schemes so that companies do not have to go through a major exercise of providing information in order to benefit from them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the one hand we want easy access, on the other hand we want effective safeguards.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These are the tensions in the administration of any Government programme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is something that Enterprise Singapore will have to wrestle with.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The last I checked, Enterprise Singapore officers, or today's IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore officers, are not caped crusaders.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They are making an effort to reach out and do the best that they can.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: What we will find as we go forward is that they will try to find this balance, adjusting their programmes and schemes according to the needs of the companies on the ground but also with an eye to Singapore's long-term economic objectives and future.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There were a series of questions on transition issues.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the unlikely event that it is not possible for certain operational reasons, the Enterprise Singapore management is committed to ensuring a seamless handover.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is important because it is not just the officer who is on the frontline, but also the team that supports him or her in the relationship with the companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I think we have enough bench strength in the system to deal with the transition issues if, in fact, there is a change of account management.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As part of any move, whether it is an enlarged role or a new one, there will be training and mentorship that is relevant that will be provided.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Enterprise Singapore will also continue to recruit officers from both the public and the private sectors because you need that blend of capabilities and they need the relevant industry and international business experience in order to support the mission.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This will include tapping on industry experts to support the enterprises through counsel advice, which is something that Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has talked about.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Patrick Tay has also asked about the integration of the cultures and workflows of the two organisations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is the perennial challenge of any merger.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The key is to get the mission clear and the leadership correct.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In the case of Enterprise Singapore, the mission is clear and, importantly, it builds on the work that has already been done by IE Singapore and SPRING Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Together, they bring extensive leadership experience in the Public Service and in working with the business community.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I am confident that they, and the senior management, will build a strong culture of the organisation and the mission orientation in Enterprise Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Even as we strengthen Enterprise Singapore in terms of its capabilities and programmes and so on, we have to ensure that the partnership and co-ownership of initiatives are something that is emphasised in the relationship with companies and industry stakeholders.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have to collectively own this and work together on it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, I agree with Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Henry Kwek that all stakeholders must work closely together to understand the challenges and also to identify the opportunities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Broadly, we are doing this in three ways.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: With the merger, Enterprise Singapore and EDB will form two critical and complementary Government agencies that will help formulate and implement strategies for the development of industry clusters and enterprises in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These agencies will also work closely with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) and JTC, among other Government organisations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we bring, first, a public sector, holistic perspective to the engagement and policies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, EDB and Enterprise Singapore will promote partnerships within the private sector, a point that has been raised by several Members.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Through the Partnerships for Capabilities Transformation (PACT) programme, they will drive greater collaboration among MNCs, LLEs, our SMEs and also our startups so that they can reinforce one another's strengths and, in the process, we end up with a competitive industry and one that is able to compete globally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Third, it is the collaboration that we have with other industry stakeholders, like TACs, which are important agents of change within industries.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Henry Kwek spoke on the need to professionalise our TACs which SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore have already been doing and supporting through the LEAD programme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We had a further evolution of that through LEAD Plus, that was introduced in Budget 2016 to strengthen the leadership and secretariat teams at the TACs and also to improve their organisational processes and deliver new value-added services.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are supporting our TACs, in terms of their people, capabilities and ability to run programmes that affect the entire industry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The points that have been raised by Mr Saktiandi Supaat in the context of SMCCI, these are the areas where they can form the agenda for engagement between Enterprise Singapore and SMCCI, for example.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The point that Ms Jessica Tan made about sharing amongst SMEs, again, it is something where you can get these collaborations going in order to see how SMEs can rely on one another and perhaps pool some of their resources.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Henry Kwek talked about the SME Centres as a first stop.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They are important nodes to provide customised business advice and help our SMEs better understand our Government initiatives.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not just about them going to SME Centres to apply for grants; it is also for SME Centres to convey and cascade information on Government programmes and initiatives.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is critical that the message reaches the entire spectrum of enterprises and I thank Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Saktiandi Supaat for their comments on public communications and strengthening outreach to SMEs and the broader public.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To promote the message of industry transformation, our agencies have engaged the target audience not only through the mainstream media but also through social media and other methods like dialogues and seminars.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They have also stepped up efforts to work with the vernacular media like Lianhe Zaobao and Berita Harian.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are working on various initiatives and we are working with the TACs and NTUC to help disseminate the message to a wider audience through their communication channels.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The TACs have organised events, such as the SBF's Future Economy conference and exhibition last year, and NTUC helps amplify messages on transformation to its network of workers through dialogues, seminars and marketing collaterals.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We value these partnerships and we want to build on them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Moving forward, Enterprise Singapore will work closely with the media, TACs and unions to propagate the transformation message to ensure greater outreach and awareness among employees.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But again, it is important that our enterprises and workers also take the initiative to find out what is happening in their industry, what the changes are, and what they need to do in order to adapt themselves to these changes and be prepared for the next phase in the development of their sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is an important responsibility that we cannot ignore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, that enterprise development has been an important component of our economic strategy, and it is an essential complement to our efforts to attract foreign investments.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, we are now in a new phase of growth, and we will need to sharpen our focus and efforts to support enterprise development and, in particular, productivity, innovation and internationalisation efforts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The future economy calls for transformation at all levels – individual, enterprise, industry and economy.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Just as the companies are being exhorted to adapt to keep pace with changes in the global economy, Government agencies and their programmes must also respond with agility to the shifting needs of industries and enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In turn, this will create greater value for our economy and good jobs and career opportunities for Singaporeans.
